sets.title: Articles & determiners · 40 items
sets.instruction: Choose the correct word. Type it in the box.

questions.q: Nadia found __________ (a / an / the) old coin under the sofa.
questions.tip: 'Old' begins with a vowel sound, so use 'an'.

questions.q: We waited for __________ (a / an / the) hour outside the clinic.
questions.tip: 'Hour' begins with a vowel sound — the h is silent.

questions.q: My uncle is __________ (a / an / the) engineer.
questions.tip: 'Engineer' begins with a vowel sound.

questions.q: She wore __________ (a / an / the) uniform to the parade.
questions.tip: 'Uniform' begins with a 'yoo' sound, which is a consonant sound.

questions.q: He has been living in Singapore for __________ (a / an / the) year.
questions.tip: 'Year' begins with a 'y' consonant sound.

questions.q: __________ (A / An / The) sun rose behind the flats.
questions.tip: There is only one sun, so use 'the'.

questions.q: I would like __________ (a / an / the) apple, please.
questions.tip: 'Apple' begins with a vowel sound.

questions.q: Mrs Lim is __________ (a / an / the) best teacher in our school.
questions.tip: Superlatives take 'the'.

questions.q: There is __________ (a / an / the) honest answer to that question.
questions.tip: The h in 'honest' is silent, so the word begins with a vowel sound.

questions.q: We go to __________ (a / the / no word) school by bus.
questions.tip: No article before 'school' when you mean attending lessons.

questions.q: My brother plays __________ (a / an / the) piano every evening.
questions.tip: Musical instruments take 'the' after 'play'.

questions.q: Rahim had __________ (a / the / no word) breakfast at half past six.
questions.tip: No article before meal names.

questions.q: __________ (A / The / no word) Singapore River runs past Clarke Quay.
questions.tip: Rivers take 'the'.

questions.q: She is __________ (a / an / the) only pupil who brought an umbrella.
questions.tip: 'Only' points to one particular person, so use 'the'.

questions.q: I bought a new bag yesterday. __________ (A / An / The) bag I chose is blue.
questions.tip: Second mention of something already introduced takes 'the'.

questions.q: How __________ (much / many / a little) eggs are left in the fridge?
questions.tip: 'Eggs' can be counted, so use 'many'.

questions.q: There isn't __________ (much / many / few) water in the bottle.
questions.tip: 'Water' cannot be counted, so use 'much'.

questions.q: Only __________ (a few / a little / much) pupils handed in their forms.
questions.tip: 'Pupils' can be counted, so use 'a few'.

questions.q: Add __________ (a few / a little / many) salt to the soup.
questions.tip: 'Salt' cannot be counted, so use 'a little'.

questions.q: I have __________ (little / few / many) money left, so I cannot buy it.
questions.tip: 'Little' without 'a' means almost none.

questions.q: __________ (Each / All / Both) of the boys has his own locker.
questions.tip: 'Has' is singular, which matches 'each'.

questions.q: __________ (Both / Each / Every) my parents work in Jurong.
questions.tip: 'Work' is plural and there are two parents.

questions.q: __________ (Every / All / Both) child received a sticker.
questions.tip: 'Child' is singular, so use 'every'.

questions.q: We have __________ (some / any / many) time before the bell.
questions.tip: Use 'some' in a positive statement.

questions.q: Is there __________ (some / any / many) milk in the cupboard?
questions.tip: Use 'any' in questions and negatives.

questions.q: She did not bring __________ (some / any / much) pencils.
questions.tip: Use 'any' after a negative.

questions.q: __________ (Neither / None / Both) of the two answers is correct — they contradict each other.
questions.tip: 'Neither' is used for two things and takes a singular verb.

questions.q: __________ (Neither / None / Both) of the five boys was chosen.
questions.tip: Use 'none' for more than two.

questions.q: I could not decide between the two, so in the end I took __________ (either / neither / both) book.
questions.tip: 'Neither' means not one and not the other of the two.

questions.q: __________ (All / Every / Each) the children enjoyed the show.
questions.tip: 'Children' is plural, so use 'all'.

questions.q: There were __________ (fewer / less / little) people at the bus stop than usual.
questions.tip: 'People' can be counted, so use 'fewer'.

questions.q: Please use __________ (fewer / less / few) sugar in your drink.
questions.tip: 'Sugar' cannot be counted, so use 'less'.

questions.q: __________ (A / An / The) information on the poster was wrong.
questions.tip: 'Information' cannot be counted, so it never takes 'a'.

questions.q: He gave me __________ (an / some / a) advice about my project.
questions.tip: 'Advice' cannot be counted, so it takes 'some' rather than 'a'.

questions.q: I need __________ (a / an / some) piece of paper.
questions.tip: 'A piece of' makes an uncountable noun countable.

questions.q: Hardly __________ (some / any / many) pupils were absent today.
questions.tip: 'Hardly' is negative in meaning, so use 'any'.

questions.q: __________ (One / Both / All) of my shoes is missing.
questions.tip: 'Is' is singular, so use 'one'.

questions.q: We visited __________ (a / an / the) Science Centre last term.
questions.tip: 'The Science Centre' is one particular place the reader already knows, so it takes 'the'.

questions.q: My grandmother goes to __________ (a / an / the) market every morning.
questions.tip: 'The market' means the one she always goes to.

questions.q: There is not __________ (much / many / few) point in arguing.
questions.tip: 'Point' here is uncountable in meaning, so use 'much'.

sets.title: Conjunctions & simple connectors · 40 items
sets.instruction: Choose the joining word that makes sense. Type it in the box.

questions.q: I wanted to play outside, __________ (and / but / so) it was raining.
questions.tip: Two ideas that disagree are joined by 'but'.

questions.q: It was raining, __________ (but / so / or) we stayed indoors.
questions.tip: 'So' introduces the result.

questions.q: She was tired __________ (because / so / but) she had walked all day.
questions.tip: 'Because' gives the reason.

questions.q: Would you like rice __________ (and / or / but) noodles?
questions.tip: 'Or' offers a choice.

questions.q: Ravi packed his bag __________ (and / but / or) tied his shoelaces.
questions.tip: Two similar actions are joined by 'and'.

questions.q: __________ (Although / Because / So) it was late, we finished the project.
questions.tip: 'Although' shows a contrast.

questions.q: We will go to the beach __________ (if / but / so) the weather is fine.
questions.tip: 'If' introduces a condition.

questions.q: Wait here __________ (until / because / so) I come back.
questions.tip: 'Until' shows up to what time.

questions.q: Hafiz ate his lunch __________ (before / because / but) he went for practice.
questions.tip: 'Before' shows which happened first.

questions.q: __________ (When / But / Or) the bell rang, everyone stood up.
questions.tip: 'When' shows the time at which something happened.

questions.q: She did not go to the party __________ (because / but / and) she was unwell.
questions.tip: 'Because' gives the reason.

questions.q: He is only seven, __________ (yet / because / so) he can swim very well.
questions.tip: 'Yet' shows a surprising contrast.

questions.q: Take an umbrella __________ (in case / because / so) it rains later.
questions.tip: 'In case' means as a precaution.

questions.q: Neither my brother __________ (or / nor / and) I could find the keys.
questions.tip: 'Neither' is always paired with 'nor'.

questions.q: Both Meiling __________ (and / or / nor) Sara joined the choir.
questions.tip: 'Both' is always paired with 'and'.

questions.q: Either you apologise __________ (and / or / nor) you leave.
questions.tip: 'Either' is always paired with 'or'.

questions.q: Not only did he win, __________ (and / but / or) he also broke the record.
questions.tip: 'Not only' is paired with 'but also'.

questions.q: I will call you __________ (as soon as / because / but) I reach home.
questions.tip: 'As soon as' means immediately after.

questions.q: The soup was too salty, __________ (but / or / because) nobody complained.
questions.tip: Two main clauses in contrast are joined by 'but'.

questions.q: __________ (Even though / Because / So) he practised daily, he did not make the team.
questions.tip: 'Even though' shows a strong contrast.

questions.q: Speak softly __________ (so that / in case / because) the baby wakes up.
questions.tip: 'In case' warns of a possibility.

questions.q: Put on your shoes __________ (so that / because / although) you can go out.
questions.tip: 'So that' shows the purpose.

questions.q: Anita reads __________ (so / because / therefore) she writes very well.
questions.tip: 'So' links a cause to its result in one sentence.

questions.q: __________ (After / Because / So) finishing his homework, Kumar washed the dishes.
questions.tip: 'After' plus -ing shows the earlier action.

questions.q: He missed the bus __________ (as / but / or) he woke up late.
questions.tip: 'As' can mean 'because'.

questions.q: We cannot leave __________ (until / because / so) everyone is ready.
questions.tip: 'Until' means not before that time.

questions.q: Jaya sings well. __________ (However / Because / And), she is shy on stage.
questions.tip: 'However' starts a new sentence and takes a comma after it.

questions.q: It was crowded. __________ (But / Because / So) we found seats in the end.
questions.tip: 'But' shows the contrast between the two sentences.

questions.q: The road was closed. __________ (Therefore / However / Although), the bus was diverted.
questions.tip: 'Therefore' shows the result.

questions.q: __________ (Either / Neither / Both) my sister nor my cousin can swim.
questions.tip: 'Neither … nor' makes both parts negative.

questions.q: She looked everywhere __________ (but / and / or) could not find her ruler.
questions.tip: The second idea contradicts the first.

questions.q: Wash your hands __________ (before / because / or) you eat, so that no dirt gets on your food.
questions.tip: The clause 'so that no dirt gets on your food' tells you the washing comes first.

questions.q: __________ (Once / Because / So) the film ended, we walked home.
questions.tip: 'Once' means as soon as.

questions.q: Hurry up, __________ (or / and / but) we will be late.
questions.tip: 'Or' warns of the consequence.

questions.q: I like durian __________ (but / because / so) my mother cannot stand it.
questions.tip: 'But' joins two ideas that disagree.

questions.q: The pupils cheered __________ (when / but / or) the goal was scored.
questions.tip: 'When' shows that the two things happened at the same moment.

questions.q: He kept quiet __________ (since / but / or) he did not want to argue.
questions.tip: 'Since' can mean 'because'.

questions.q: __________ (Although / However / Because) she tried very hard, she could not open the jar.
questions.tip: 'Although' shows a contrast and comes at the start of the clause.

questions.q: Bring a jacket __________ (as / but / or) the hall is cold.
questions.tip: 'As' gives the reason.

questions.q: We had no money left, __________ (so / because / although) we walked home.
questions.tip: 'So' gives the result.

sets.title: Subject–verb agreement · harder cases
sets.instruction: These are the cases pupils get wrong most often at Primary 6. Choose the correct verb.

questions.q: The list of names __________ (is / are) on the noticeboard.
questions.tip: The subject is 'list', not 'names'.

questions.q: A bunch of keys __________ (has / have) been left on the table.
questions.tip: The subject is 'bunch'.

questions.q: Neither the coach nor the players __________ (was / were) satisfied.
questions.tip: With 'neither … nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'players'.

questions.q: Neither the players nor the coach __________ (was / were) satisfied.
questions.tip: The nearer subject is now 'coach', which is singular.

questions.q: Every one of the answers __________ (is / are) wrong.
questions.tip: The subject is 'every one'.

questions.q: Economics __________ (is / are) taught only in secondary school.
questions.tip: Subjects ending in -ics take a singular verb.

questions.q: The scissors __________ (is / are) in the top drawer.
questions.tip: 'Scissors' is always plural.

questions.q: Ten dollars __________ (is / are) too much for a pencil case.
questions.tip: An amount of money is treated as one thing.

questions.q: Three quarters of the cake __________ (has / have) been eaten.
questions.tip: 'Cake' is uncountable, so the fraction is singular.

questions.q: Three quarters of the pupils __________ (has / have) arrived.
questions.tip: 'Pupils' is plural, so the fraction is plural.

questions.q: There __________ (is / are) a pen and two rulers on the desk.
questions.tip: With a compound subject, careful written English uses 'are'. You will also hear 'There is a pen and two rulers', which follows the nearer noun.

questions.q: Here __________ (is / are) the photographs you asked for.
questions.tip: The subject is 'photographs'.

questions.q: The number of complaints __________ (is / are) falling.
questions.tip: 'The number' is singular.

questions.q: A number of complaints __________ (has / have) been received.
questions.tip: 'A number of' means several, so it is plural.

questions.q: My aunt, together with her two sons, __________ (is / are) visiting us.
questions.tip: 'Together with' does not change the subject.

questions.q: Rice and curry __________ (is / are) my usual lunch.
questions.tip: 'Rice and curry' is one dish.

questions.q: The bread and butter __________ (is / are) on the tray.
questions.tip: 'Bread and butter' is treated as a single item.

questions.q: Each of the twins __________ (has / have) a different bicycle.
questions.tip: 'Each' is singular.

questions.q: Both of the twins __________ (has / have) bicycles.
questions.tip: 'Both' is plural.

questions.q: One of my shoes __________ (is / are) missing.
questions.tip: The subject is 'one'.

questions.q: The committee __________ (is / are) meeting this afternoon.
questions.tip: A committee acting as one body takes a singular verb.

questions.q: Physics and chemistry __________ (is / are) taught in the same room.
questions.tip: Two separate subjects make a plural.

questions.q: Nobody in the class __________ (knows / know) the answer.
questions.tip: 'Nobody' is singular.

questions.q: Everybody __________ (has / have) their own opinion on this.
questions.tip: 'Everybody' is singular.

questions.q: Somebody __________ (has / have) left the tap running.
questions.tip: 'Somebody' is singular.

questions.q: The police __________ (is / are) still searching for the owner.
questions.tip: 'Police' is treated as plural.

questions.q: A pair of gloves __________ (has / have) been left behind.
questions.tip: The subject is 'pair'.

questions.q: The furniture in the hall __________ (is / are) very old.
questions.tip: 'Furniture' is uncountable.

questions.q: My trousers __________ (is / are) too short now.
questions.tip: 'Trousers' is always plural.

questions.q: Either of the two answers __________ (is / are) acceptable, according to the marking scheme.
questions.tip: 'Either' means one of the two, so it is singular.

questions.q: Half of the water __________ (has / have) evaporated.
questions.tip: 'Water' is uncountable.

questions.q: Half of the bottles __________ (is / are) empty.
questions.tip: 'Bottles' is plural.

questions.q: The teacher, as well as the pupils, __________ (was / were) pleased.
questions.tip: 'As well as' does not change the subject.

questions.q: Measles __________ (is / are) a serious illness in young children.
questions.tip: Illnesses ending in -es like 'measles' are singular.

questions.q: Twenty kilometres __________ (is / are) a long way to cycle.
questions.tip: A single distance is treated as one thing.

questions.q: There __________ (was / were) nobody left in the hall.
questions.tip: 'Nobody' is singular.

questions.q: Not one of the answers __________ (was / were) correct.
questions.tip: 'Not one' is singular.

questions.q: Most of the pupils __________ (has / have) handed in their forms.
questions.tip: 'Pupils' is plural, so the fraction word takes a plural verb.

questions.q: The cost of the tickets __________ (has / have) risen again.
questions.tip: The subject is 'cost'.

questions.q: Neither of my parents __________ (lets / let) me go.
questions.tip: 'Neither' is singular, so the verb takes -s.

questions.q: This bag is __________ than mine.
questions.tip: One-syllable and two-syllable words ending in -y take -er.

questions.q: Of all the pupils, Jun Hao is the __________.
questions.tip: Comparing three or more takes the superlative with 'the'.

questions.q: Durians are __________ expensive than mangoes.
questions.tip: Long adjectives take 'more' for the comparative.

questions.q: That was the __________ film I have ever seen.
questions.tip: Comparing against all films needs the superlative.

questions.q: Her handwriting is __________ than her brother's.
questions.tip: 'Neat' is short, so add -er.

questions.q: Today is __________ than yesterday.
questions.tip: Double the t before adding -er.

questions.q: This is the __________ book on the shelf.
questions.tip: Double the n before -est.

questions.q: My results this term are __________ than last term's.
questions.tip: 'Good' becomes 'better'.

questions.q: He plays the guitar __________ than I do.
questions.tip: Comparing two actions needs 'better', not 'well'.

questions.q: This is the __________ I have ever felt.
questions.tip: 'Bad' becomes 'worse' then 'worst'.

questions.q: The queue moved __________ than we expected.
questions.tip: Adverbs ending in -ly take 'more'.

questions.q: Of the three sisters, Mei Lin runs __________.
questions.tip: 'Fast' is both adjective and adverb; the superlative is 'fastest'.

questions.q: There were __________ people at the fair this year.
questions.tip: 'People' can be counted, so use 'fewer'.

questions.q: I have __________ homework today than yesterday.
questions.tip: 'Homework' cannot be counted, so use 'less'.

questions.q: This road is __________ of the two.
questions.tip: With only two things, use 'the' plus the comparative.

questions.q: She is __________ girl in the choir.
questions.tip: Superlatives need 'the'.

questions.q: My bag is not as __________ as yours.
questions.tip: 'As … as' takes the plain adjective.

questions.q: The blue shirt costs __________ the red one.
questions.tip: The pattern is 'twice as much as'.

questions.q: His story was __________ interesting of all.
questions.tip: Superlative of a long adjective is 'the most'.

questions.q: The __________ you start, the sooner you will finish.
questions.tip: The 'the … the' pattern uses two comparatives.

questions.q: Nothing is __________ than being ignored.
questions.tip: Comparing two things needs 'worse'.

questions.q: She sang __________ beautifully than the soloist.
questions.tip: Adverbs in -ly take 'more'.

questions.q: This puzzle is __________ difficult of the three.
questions.tip: Three items need the superlative with 'the'.

questions.q: He is __________ older than his cousin.
questions.tip: 'Much' strengthens a comparative; 'very' cannot.

questions.q: Of the two answers, this one is __________.
questions.tip: Two things take the comparative.

questions.q: My sister is __________ as tall as me.
questions.tip: 'Almost as … as' works; 'more as' does not.

questions.q: The weather today is far __________ than yesterday.
questions.tip: 'Pleasant' is a long adjective, so use 'more'.

questions.q: He arrived __________ of all the guests.
questions.tip: A superlative adverb normally has no 'the': 'fastest', 'latest', 'hardest'.

questions.q: This shop has the __________ prices in the mall.
questions.tip: Comparing all shops needs the superlative.

questions.q: A cheetah runs __________ than a horse.
questions.tip: Comparing two takes 'faster'.

questions.q: Your drawing is as __________ as the one in the book.
questions.tip: 'As … as' takes the plain adjective 'good'.

questions.q: That was the __________ meal I have eaten all week.
questions.tip: -y becomes -iest in the superlative.

questions.q: He is the __________ of the four brothers.
questions.tip: Four brothers means the superlative.

questions.q: My marks are __________ worse than I hoped.
questions.tip: Use 'much' before a comparative.

questions.q: This is __________ crowded than the other train.
questions.tip: 'Less crowded' is the comparative of 'crowded' going downwards.

questions.q: The __________ we walked, the hungrier we became.
questions.tip: 'Far' becomes 'farther'.

questions.q: Nobody in the class writes __________ than Devi.
questions.tip: Comparing two writers needs the comparative adverb.

questions.q: It was the __________ decision he had ever made.
questions.tip: 'Wise' takes -est.

questions.q: These shoes are __________ comfortable than those.
questions.tip: 'Less comfortable' is the correct downward comparative.

questions.q: Of all the days of the week, Monday feels the __________.
questions.tip: Comparing seven days needs the superlative.

sets.title: Verb patterns · gerunds & infinitives
sets.instruction: After some verbs we use the -ing form, and after others we use 'to'. Type the correct form.

questions.q: She enjoys __________ (sing / to sing / singing) in the school choir.
questions.tip: 'Enjoy' is always followed by -ing.

questions.q: He decided __________ (tell / to tell / telling) the truth.
questions.tip: 'Decide' is followed by 'to'.

questions.q: Would you mind __________ (close / to close / closing) the window?
questions.tip: 'Mind' is followed by -ing.

questions.q: They agreed __________ (share / to share / sharing) the cost.
questions.tip: 'Agree' is followed by 'to'.

questions.q: I have finished __________ (write / to write / writing) my essay.
questions.tip: 'Finish' is followed by -ing.

questions.q: We hope __________ (see / to see / seeing) you at the concert.
questions.tip: 'Hope' is followed by 'to'.

questions.q: Avoid __________ (eat / to eat / eating) heavy meals before swimming.
questions.tip: 'Avoid' is followed by -ing.

questions.q: She promised __________ (be / to be / being) on time.
questions.tip: 'Promise' is followed by 'to'.

questions.q: He kept __________ (run / to run / running) even though his legs ached.
questions.tip: 'Keep' is followed by -ing.

questions.q: My father taught me __________ (ride / to ride / riding) a bicycle.
questions.tip: 'Teach someone' is followed by 'to'.

questions.q: Do you fancy __________ (go / to go / going) for a swim?
questions.tip: 'Fancy' is followed by -ing.

questions.q: The boys refused __________ (tidy / to tidy / tidying) the room.
questions.tip: 'Refuse' is followed by 'to'.

questions.q: I look forward to __________ (hear / to hear / hearing) from you.
questions.tip: 'Look forward to' is followed by -ing.

questions.q: She managed __________ (get / to get / getting) the jar open.
questions.tip: 'Manage' is followed by 'to'.

questions.q: Imagine __________ (live / to live / living) in a treehouse.
questions.tip: 'Imagine' is followed by -ing.

questions.q: He offered __________ (carry / to carry / carrying) my bag.
questions.tip: 'Offer' is followed by 'to'.

questions.q: We are used to __________ (wake / to wake / waking) up early.
questions.tip: 'Be used to' is followed by -ing.

questions.q: The doctor advised him __________ (drink / to drink / drinking) more water.
questions.tip: 'Advise someone' is followed by 'to'.

questions.q: She is thinking of __________ (try / to try / trying) for the netball team.
questions.tip: A preposition such as 'of' is followed by -ing.

questions.q: I would rather __________ (stay / to stay / staying) at home tonight.
questions.tip: 'Would rather' is followed by the plain verb.

questions.q: They made me __________ (repeat / to repeat / repeating) my apology.
questions.tip: 'Make someone' is followed by the plain verb.

questions.q: Let him __________ (find / to find / finding) the answer himself.
questions.tip: 'Let' is followed by the plain verb.

questions.q: He was allowed __________ (leave / to leave / leaving) the hall early.
questions.tip: 'Be allowed' is followed by 'to'.

questions.q: I cannot help __________ (worry / to worry / worrying) about the results.
questions.tip: 'Cannot help' is followed by -ing.

questions.q: She pretended __________ (be / to be / being) asleep.
questions.tip: 'Pretend' is followed by 'to'.

questions.q: It is no use __________ (complain / to complain / complaining) about it now.
questions.tip: 'It is no use' is followed by -ing.

questions.q: We had better __________ (leave / to leave / leaving) before it rains.
questions.tip: 'Had better' is followed by the plain verb.

questions.q: Stop __________ (tap / to tap / tapping) your pen on the desk.
questions.tip: 'Stop' plus -ing means stop that action.

questions.q: On the way home we stopped __________ (buy / to buy / buying) some bread.
questions.tip: 'Stop to' means stop in order to do something.

questions.q: I remember __________ (lock / to lock / locking) the door before we left.
questions.tip: 'Remember' plus -ing means recalling a past action.

questions.q: Please remember __________ (post / to post / posting) the letter.
questions.tip: 'Remember to' means do not forget to do it.

questions.q: She suggested __________ (postpone / to postpone / postponing) the meeting.
questions.tip: 'Suggest' is followed by -ing.

questions.q: The children were busy __________ (make / to make / making) their costumes.
questions.tip: 'Busy' is followed by -ing.

questions.q: He apologised for __________ (arrive / to arrive / arriving) late.
questions.tip: The preposition 'for' is followed by -ing.

questions.q: There is nothing left __________ (do / to do / doing).
questions.tip: After 'nothing left' we use 'to'.

questions.q: I am learning __________ (play / to play / playing) the guzheng.
questions.tip: 'Learn' is followed by 'to'.

questions.q: Would you like __________ (have / to have / having) some tea?
questions.tip: 'Would like' is followed by 'to'.

questions.q: He denied __________ (break / to break / breaking) the vase.
questions.tip: 'Deny' is followed by -ing.

questions.q: We must practise __________ (say / to say / saying) our lines before Friday.
questions.tip: 'Practise' is followed by -ing.

questions.q: Do not forget __________ (bring / to bring / bringing) your water bottle.
questions.tip: 'Forget to' means do not fail to do it.

sets.title: Conditionals · if-clauses
sets.instruction: Type the correct form of the verb so that the sentence follows the pattern for its type of 'if'.

questions.q: If you heat ice, it __________ (melt / melts / will melt).
questions.tip: For things always true, use the present in both halves.

questions.q: If it rains tomorrow, we __________ (cancel / will cancel / cancelled) the match.
questions.tip: Likely future: present tense in the if-clause, 'will' in the other.

questions.q: If I __________ (am / was / were) you, I would apologise.
questions.tip: For imagining, use 'were' with 'I'.

questions.q: If she studies harder, she __________ (get / will get / would get) better results.
questions.tip: A real possibility takes 'will'.

questions.q: If I had a bicycle, I __________ (cycle / will cycle / would cycle) to school.
questions.tip: Imagining an unreal present takes 'would'.

questions.q: If you press this button, the light __________ (come / comes / will come) on.
questions.tip: A general fact takes the present tense.

questions.q: If he __________ (left / had left / leaves) earlier, he would not have missed the bus.
questions.tip: Regret about the past takes 'had' plus the past participle.

questions.q: If they had asked me, I __________ (will have / would have / had) helped.
questions.tip: The past unreal pattern is 'would have' plus the past participle.

questions.q: We will go to the beach if the weather __________ (is / will be / were) fine.
questions.tip: Do not use 'will' in the if-clause.

questions.q: If I __________ (know / knew / had known) the answer, I would tell you.
questions.tip: Imagining the present takes the past tense in the if-clause.

questions.q: If you do not water the plant, it __________ (die / dies / will die).
questions.tip: A likely result takes 'will'.

questions.q: If my brother __________ (is / was / were) taller, he could reach the shelf.
questions.tip: Imagining takes 'were' in careful written English.

questions.q: If we had known about the jam, we __________ (took / would take / would have taken) the train.
questions.tip: The past is unreal, so use 'would have taken'.

questions.q: Unless you hurry, you __________ (miss / will miss / would miss) the beginning.
questions.tip: 'Unless' means 'if not' and takes the same pattern as a likely future.

questions.q: If she __________ (calls / had called / would call) me, I would have replied.
questions.tip: The if-clause about the past takes 'had called'.

questions.q: Water boils if you __________ (heat / heats / will heat) it to a hundred degrees.
questions.tip: 'You heat' is the present tense for a general truth.

questions.q: If I were rich, I __________ (build / will build / would build) a library for my school.
questions.tip: This is imagining, so use 'would'.

questions.q: If the bus __________ (is / will be / were) late again, we shall complain.
questions.tip: Keep 'will' out of the if-clause.

questions.q: He would have won if he __________ (did not give / had not given / would not give) up.
questions.tip: The past unreal if-clause takes 'had not given'.

questions.q: If you mix blue and yellow, you __________ (get / will get / would get) green.
questions.tip: A scientific fact takes the present in both halves.

questions.q: If I __________ (know / knew / had known) how to swim, I would join the team.
questions.tip: He does not know now, so use the past tense.

questions.q: If she had studied, she __________ (will have / would have / had) passed.
questions.tip: Use 'would have' plus the past participle.

questions.q: I will lend you my book provided you __________ (bring / will bring / brought) it back.
questions.tip: 'Provided' behaves like 'if' and takes the present.

questions.q: If the lift __________ (was not / had not been / were not) working, we would have used the stairs.
questions.tip: The past unreal takes 'had not been'.

questions.q: __________ (If / Unless / Should) you have any problems, please call me.
questions.tip: 'If' introduces the condition. (In very formal writing you may also see 'Should you have any problems'.)

questions.q: If I were you, I __________ (delete / will delete / would delete) that message.
questions.tip: 'If I were you' is always followed by 'would'.

questions.q: The alarm rings if smoke __________ (reach / reaches / will reach) the sensor.
questions.tip: 'Smoke' is singular, and a general truth takes the present.

questions.q: If we leave now, we __________ (are / will be / would be) there by six.
questions.tip: A real plan takes 'will'.

questions.q: If he __________ (trained / had trained / would train) harder last year, he would be in the team now.
questions.tip: The cause is in the past, so use 'had trained'.

questions.q: I would not have said that if I __________ (knew / had known / would know) she was listening.
questions.tip: Regret about the past takes 'had known'.

sets.title: Punctuating speech & dialogue · 30 items
sets.instruction: Rewrite each line with the correct punctuation and capital letters. Then compare with the model.

questions.q: Add punctuation: i am not going said rachel
questions.tip: The comma goes inside the closing quotation marks, and the speaker's name follows.

questions.q: Add punctuation: where did you put my calculator asked ben
questions.m: "Where did you put my calculator?" asked Ben.
a: "Where did you put my calculator?" asked Ben.
questions.tip: A question keeps its question mark inside the quotation marks; no comma is added.

questions.q: Add punctuation: mrs tan shouted get out of the pool now
questions.m: Mrs Tan shouted, "Get out of the pool now!"
a: Mrs Tan shouted, "Get out of the pool now!"
questions.tip: When the speaker comes first, a comma goes before the opening quotation mark.

questions.q: Add punctuation: that is unfair muttered devi under her breath
questions.m: "That is unfair," muttered Devi under her breath.
a: "That is unfair," muttered Devi under her breath.
questions.tip: The reporting clause may carry extra detail after the verb.

questions.q: Add punctuation: i finished it she said last night
questions.tip: When speech is split, both halves are in quotation marks and the second half starts in lower case.

questions.q: Add punctuation: hurry up he yelled the bus is leaving
questions.m: "Hurry up!" he yelled. "The bus is leaving."
a: "Hurry up!" he yelled. "The bus is leaving."
questions.tip: Two separate sentences of speech each need their own full stop.

questions.q: Add punctuation: my father asked whether i had eaten
questions.m: My father asked whether I had eaten.
a: My father asked whether I had eaten.
questions.tip: Reported speech takes no quotation marks at all.

questions.q: Add punctuation: the sign read no entry after six
questions.m: The sign read: "No entry after six."
a: The sign read: "No entry after six."
questions.tip: A colon may introduce written words being quoted.

questions.q: Add punctuation: i cant find it anywhere she wailed
questions.m: "I can't find it anywhere," she wailed.
a: "I can't find it anywhere," she wailed.
questions.tip: The apostrophe in 'can\'t' replaces the missing o of 'not'.

questions.q: Add punctuation: well said the coach that was better
questions.tip: 'Well' is an interjection, so it takes a comma inside the quotation marks.

questions.q: Add punctuation: did you hear that whispered ahmad
questions.tip: Keep the question mark and do not add a comma after it.

questions.q: Add punctuation: stop the teacher said firmly
questions.tip: A command spoken sharply takes an exclamation mark inside the quotation marks.

questions.q: Add punctuation: she replied that she would think about it
questions.m: She replied that she would think about it.
a: She replied that she would think about it.
questions.tip: 'That' signals reported speech, so no quotation marks are used.

questions.q: Add punctuation: the boys shouted we won we won
questions.m: The boys shouted, "We won! We won!"
a: The boys shouted, "We won! We won!"
questions.tip: Both exclamations sit inside one pair of quotation marks.

questions.q: Add punctuation: are you sure asked mother i thought it was tomorrow
questions.m: "Are you sure?" asked Mother. "I thought it was tomorrow."
a: "Are you sure?" asked Mother. "I thought it was tomorrow."
questions.tip: A new sentence of speech begins after the reporting clause.

questions.q: Add punctuation: no he said i never said that
questions.tip: The second half continues the same sentence, so it opens with a lower-case word unless it is 'I'.

questions.q: Punctuate the list: i packed my goggles a towel sunblock and my swimming cap
questions.m: I packed my goggles, a towel, sunblock and my swimming cap.
a: I packed my goggles, a towel, sunblock and my swimming cap.
questions.tip: Commas separate items in a list; the last two are joined by 'and'.

questions.q: Punctuate: although it was raining we still walked to school
questions.m: Although it was raining, we still walked to school.
a: Although it was raining, we still walked to school.
questions.tip: A comma follows an opening subordinate clause.

questions.q: Punctuate: my cousin who lives in perth is visiting us
questions.m: My cousin, who lives in Perth, is visiting us.
a: My cousin, who lives in Perth, is visiting us.
questions.tip: Extra information is enclosed in a pair of commas.

questions.q: Punctuate: the answer was obvious nobody had checked the plug
questions.m: The answer was obvious: nobody had checked the plug.
a: The answer was obvious: nobody had checked the plug.
questions.tip: A colon introduces an explanation of what came before.

questions.q: Punctuate: we had two choices wait or walk
questions.m: We had two choices: wait or walk.
a: We had two choices: wait or walk.
questions.tip: A colon introduces the choices being announced.

questions.q: Punctuate: the hall was full however we found seats
questions.m: The hall was full; however, we found seats.
a: The hall was full; however, we found seats.
questions.tip: A semicolon joins two complete sentences, and 'however' takes a comma after it.

questions.q: Punctuate: the dogs bowl was empty
questions.tip: One dog owns the bowl, so the apostrophe goes before the s.

questions.q: Punctuate: the boys changing room was locked to all twelve of them
questions.m: The boys' changing room was locked to all twelve of them.
a: The boys' changing room was locked to all twelve of them.
questions.tip: The room belongs to more than one boy, so the apostrophe goes after the s.

questions.q: Punctuate: its raining and the cat has hurt its paw
questions.m: It's raining and the cat has hurt its paw.
a: It's raining and the cat has hurt its paw.
questions.tip: 'It's' means 'it is'; the possessive 'its' has no apostrophe.

questions.q: Punctuate: my brothers bicycles were both stolen he owns two
questions.m: My brother's bicycles were both stolen; he owns two.
a: My brother's bicycles were both stolen; he owns two.
questions.tip: One brother owns two bicycles, so the apostrophe goes before the s.

questions.q: Punctuate: mr lee our form teacher retires in june
questions.m: Mr Lee, our form teacher, retires in June.
a: Mr Lee, our form teacher, retires in June.
questions.tip: The description of Mr Lee sits between a pair of commas.

questions.q: Punctuate: what a mess the boys had made
questions.m: What a mess the boys had made!
a: What a mess the boys had made!
questions.tip: An exclamation beginning with 'What a' ends with an exclamation mark.

questions.q: Punctuate: i was tired therefore i went to bed early
questions.m: I was tired; therefore, I went to bed early.
a: I was tired; therefore, I went to bed early.
questions.tip: Two complete sentences joined by 'therefore' need a semicolon, not a comma.

questions.q: Punctuate: please bring the following a pencil a ruler and an eraser
questions.m: Please bring the following: a pencil, a ruler and an eraser.
a: Please bring the following: a pencil, a ruler and an eraser.
questions.tip: A colon introduces a list announced by 'the following'.

sets.title: Synthesis & transformation · 40 more
sets.instruction: Rewrite as one sentence using the word or words given. The meaning must not change. Then compare with the model.

questions.q: The boy was very short. He could not reach the top shelf. **(too)**
questions.m: The boy was too short to reach the top shelf
a: The boy was too short to reach the top shelf
questions.tip: 'Too … to' replaces 'very … could not'.

questions.q: Ravi apologised. He had broken the window. **(for)**
questions.m: Ravi apologised for breaking the window
a: Ravi apologised for breaking the window
questions.tip: 'For' is followed by the -ing form.

questions.q: "I will return the book tomorrow," said Mei. **(that)**
questions.m: Mei said that she would return the book the following day
a: Mei said that she would return the book the following day
questions.tip: In reported speech 'will' becomes 'would' and 'tomorrow' becomes 'the following day'.

questions.q: The concert was cancelled. The singer was ill. **(because of)**
questions.m: The concert was cancelled because of the singer's illness
a: The concert was cancelled because of the singer's illness
questions.tip: 'Because of' is followed by a noun, not a clause.

questions.q: She started learning the violin five years ago. She still plays it. **(for)**
questions.m: She has been playing the violin for five years
a: She has been playing the violin for five years
questions.tip: A situation continuing until now takes the present perfect continuous.

questions.q: Nobody helped him. He finished the model alone. **(without)**
questions.m: He finished the model without anybody's help
a: He finished the model without anybody's help
questions.tip: 'Without' is followed by a noun phrase.

questions.q: The soup was too salty. Nobody could finish it. **(so … that)**
questions.m: The soup was so salty that nobody could finish it
a: The soup was so salty that nobody could finish it
questions.tip: 'So … that' keeps the clause structure.

questions.q: It began to rain. We were halfway up the hill. **(when)**
questions.m: It began to rain when we were halfway up the hill
a: It began to rain when we were halfway up the hill
questions.tip: 'When' joins the two events.

questions.q: He did not study. He failed the test. **(consequently)**
questions.m: He did not study; consequently, he failed the test
a: He did not study; consequently, he failed the test
questions.tip: 'Consequently' needs a semicolon before it and a comma after.

questions.q: "Have you finished your homework?" Mother asked me. **(whether)**
questions.m: Mother asked me whether I had finished my homework
a: Mother asked me whether I had finished my homework
questions.tip: A reported question drops the question mark and the inversion.

questions.q: The film was so frightening. I could not sleep afterwards. **(such)**
questions.m: It was such a frightening film that I could not sleep afterwards
a: It was such a frightening film that I could not sleep afterwards
questions.tip: 'Such' goes before a noun; 'so' goes before an adjective alone.

questions.q: They will paint the classroom next week. **(will be)**
questions.m: The classroom will be painted next week
a: The classroom will be painted next week
questions.tip: The passive of 'will paint' is 'will be painted'.

questions.q: Someone stole my bicycle last night. **(was)**
questions.m: My bicycle was stolen last night
a: My bicycle was stolen last night
questions.tip: In the passive the doer may be dropped when unknown.

questions.q: The examination is difficult. Few pupils pass it at the first attempt. **(such)**
questions.m: It is such a difficult examination that few pupils pass it at the first attempt
a: It is such a difficult examination that few pupils pass it at the first attempt
questions.tip: 'Such a' plus adjective plus noun.

questions.q: I have never eaten a hotter curry. **(the hottest)**
questions.m: This is the hottest curry I have ever eaten
a: This is the hottest curry I have ever eaten
questions.tip: 'Never … a hotter' becomes 'the hottest … ever'.

questions.q: He is not old enough to watch that film. **(too)**
questions.m: He is too young to watch that film
a: He is too young to watch that film
questions.tip: 'Not old enough' becomes 'too young'.

questions.q: As soon as the bell rang, the pupils left. **(No sooner)**
questions.m: No sooner had the bell rung than the pupils left
a: No sooner had the bell rung than the pupils left
questions.tip: 'No sooner' inverts the verb and is paired with 'than'.

questions.q: She is a careful driver. **(carefully)**
questions.tip: The adjective becomes an adverb and the noun becomes a verb.

questions.q: Although he was tired, he kept going. **(despite)**
questions.m: Despite being tired, he kept going
a: Despite being tired, he kept going
questions.tip: 'Despite' is followed by a noun or -ing form, never a clause.

questions.q: The last time I saw her was in March. **(since)**
questions.m: I have not seen her since March
a: I have not seen her since March
questions.tip: 'The last time' becomes a negative present perfect with 'since'.

questions.q: Wear a helmet. You may be fined. **(unless)**
questions.m: Unless you wear a helmet, you may be fined
a: Unless you wear a helmet, you may be fined
questions.tip: 'Unless' means 'if you do not'.

questions.q: He cannot swim. His sister cannot swim either. **(Neither)**
questions.m: Neither he nor his sister can swim
a: Neither he nor his sister can swim
questions.tip: 'Neither … nor' makes the sentence negative, so 'cannot' becomes 'can'.

questions.q: The hall was full of parents. There was nowhere to sit. **(so many)**
questions.m: There were so many parents in the hall that there was nowhere to sit
a: There were so many parents in the hall that there was nowhere to sit
questions.tip: 'So many' is used with countable nouns.

questions.q: He was the only pupil who noticed. **(apart from)**
questions.m: Apart from him, no pupil noticed
a: Apart from him, no pupil noticed
questions.tip: 'Apart from' plus a negative statement keeps the meaning.

questions.q: She sings better than anyone else in the choir. **(the best)**
questions.m: She is the best singer in the choir
a: She is the best singer in the choir
questions.tip: A comparative against everyone becomes a superlative.

questions.q: "Do not touch the wet paint," the workman warned us. **(not to)**
questions.m: The workman warned us not to touch the wet paint
a: The workman warned us not to touch the wet paint
questions.tip: A reported command uses 'not to' plus the plain verb.

questions.q: It is three years since I last visited Penang. **(have not)**
questions.m: I have not visited Penang for three years
a: I have not visited Penang for three years
questions.tip: 'It is … since' becomes a negative present perfect with 'for'.

questions.q: The queue was long. We decided to come back later. **(such a)**
questions.m: It was such a long queue that we decided to come back later
a: It was such a long queue that we decided to come back later
questions.tip: 'Such a' plus adjective plus noun plus 'that'.

questions.q: He plays the piano. He also composes music. **(not only)**
questions.m: Not only does he play the piano but he also composes music
a: Not only does he play the piano but he also composes music
questions.tip: 'Not only' at the start inverts the verb with 'does'.

questions.q: Nobody expected the result. **(unexpected)**
questions.tip: The negative becomes an adjective with a negative prefix.

questions.q: They are building a new library. It will open in June. **(which)**
questions.m: They are building a new library, which will open in June
a: They are building a new library, which will open in June
questions.tip: 'Which' after a comma adds extra information about the noun 'library'.

questions.q: I was too nervous to speak. **(so … that)**
questions.m: I was so nervous that I could not speak
a: I was so nervous that I could not speak
questions.tip: 'Too … to' becomes 'so … that' plus a negative.

questions.q: The road is being widened. It has been closed to traffic. **(As)**
questions.m: As the road is being widened, it has been closed to traffic
a: As the road is being widened, it has been closed to traffic
questions.tip: 'As' means 'because' here.

questions.q: She did not tell me. I did not know she had moved. **(Had)**
questions.m: Had she told me, I would have known she had moved
a: Had she told me, I would have known she had moved
questions.tip: 'Had' at the start replaces 'if … had' in a past conditional.

questions.q: The museum is closed on Mondays. **(does not open)**
questions.m: The museum does not open on Mondays
a: The museum does not open on Mondays
questions.tip: 'Is closed' becomes the active negative 'does not open'.

questions.q: His explanation was not clear. **(failed)**
questions.m: His explanation failed to make things clear
a: His explanation failed to make things clear
questions.tip: 'Failed to' is a formal way of saying 'did not'.

questions.q: Only after the bell did I remember my bag. **(until)**
questions.m: I did not remember my bag until the bell rang
a: I did not remember my bag until the bell rang
questions.tip: 'Only after' becomes 'not … until'.

questions.q: Everybody was tired. Nobody complained. **(although)**
questions.m: Although everybody was tired, nobody complained
a: Although everybody was tired, nobody complained
questions.tip: 'Although' introduces the contrast and takes a comma.

questions.q: The boy who won the prize is my neighbour. **(winner)**
questions.m: The winner of the prize is my neighbour
a: The winner of the prize is my neighbour
questions.tip: A relative clause can often be shortened to a noun phrase.

questions.q: This is the last time I shall warn you. **(again)**
questions.m: I shall not warn you again
a: I shall not warn you again
questions.tip: 'The last time' becomes a negative with 'again'.

sets.title: Spelling · 40 more words
sets.instruction: Type the missing word, spelt correctly. These are the words most often misspelt in Primary 4 to 6 compositions.

questions.q: It is __________ to bring your own water bottle.
questions.tip: One c, two s's: ne-ces-sary.

questions.q: I will __________ be there before six.
questions.tip: There is no 'a' in 'definitely' — it comes from 'finite'.

questions.q: Keep the wet clothes __________ from the dry ones.
questions.tip: There is 'a rat' in sep-a-rate.

questions.q: He was __________ when his voice cracked.
questions.tip: Two r's and two s's.

questions.q: At the __________ of the term we chose monitors.
questions.tip: Double the n before -ing.

questions.q: The stain did not __________ after washing.
questions.tip: One s, two p's: dis + appear.

questions.q: We must protect the __________.
questions.tip: There is an n before the m: environ-ment.

questions.q: The laws of a country are made by its __________.
questions.tip: There is an n before the m: govern-ment.

questions.q: We ate at a small __________ near the pier.
questions.tip: -aurant at the end, not -aurent.

questions.q: The drummer kept a steady __________.
questions.tip: Two h's and no vowel between the r and the y.

questions.q: It was a special __________ for our family.
questions.tip: Two c's, one s.

questions.q: It was a __________ to be chosen.
questions.tip: No d: pri-vi-lege.

questions.q: I would __________ this book to anyone.
questions.tip: One c, two m's.

questions.q: The change was __________ within a week.
questions.tip: Keep the e of 'notice' before -able.

questions.q: They had an __________ about the score.
questions.tip: Drop the e of 'argue' before -ment.

questions.q: I am __________ sorry for what I said.
questions.tip: Drop the e of 'true' before -ly.

questions.q: I __________ she is telling the truth.
questions.tip: i before e, except after c.

questions.q: Did you __________ my message?
questions.tip: e before i after c.

questions.q: She worked hard to __________ her goal.
questions.tip: i before e here.

questions.q: There was a __________ smell in the store room.
questions.tip: 'Weird' breaks the rule: e before i.

questions.q: Our __________ lent us a ladder.
questions.tip: -eigh- in the middle, and -our in British spelling.

questions.q: My mother and her __________ share an office at work.
questions.tip: -eague at the end: col-league.

questions.q: We joined the __________ outside the hall.
questions.tip: Four vowels in a row after the q: q-u-e-u-e.

questions.q: Eat at least one __________ at every meal.
questions.tip: Three syllables in writing: veg-e-table.

questions.q: The __________ dropped suddenly at night.
questions.tip: Do not lose the -era- in the middle.

questions.q: She returned the books to the __________.
questions.tip: Two r's: lib-rar-y.

questions.q: My birthday falls in __________.
questions.tip: There is an r before the u.

questions.q: Assembly is held on __________.
questions.tip: There is a silent d: Wed-nes-day.

questions.q: We do this __________ every morning.
questions.tip: -cise at the end, not -size.

questions.q: The party was a complete __________.
questions.tip: Two r's: sur-prise.

questions.q: My uncle studied accounting and now runs his own __________.
questions.tip: busi-ness, from 'busy'.

questions.q: The __________ met on Friday.
questions.tip: Two m's, two t's, two e's.

questions.q: Please come __________ after the bell.
questions.tip: Two m's, and -ately at the end.

questions.q: Do not __________ when someone is speaking.
questions.tip: Two r's: inter + rupt.

questions.q: Her attempt was __________ on the third try.
questions.tip: Two c's, two s's, one l.

questions.q: Wait here __________ I return.
questions.tip: Only one l in 'until'.

questions.q: We __________ found the missing key.
questions.tip: Two l's: final + ly.

questions.q: Our answers were very __________.
questions.tip: -ar at the end, not -er.

questions.q: He had a __________ ache all morning.
questions.tip: -ach at the end, pronounced 'ak'.

questions.q: Pass me the __________, please.
questions.tip: Silent c at the start, and a double s in the middle: sci-ssors.

sets.title: Editing · four more passages
sets.instruction: Each line has one error. Type the correction only — the single word that should replace the wrong one.

questions.q: Passage 14 — Last December my family drive up to Malacca for three days.
questions.tip: The error was “drive”. The sentence is about last December, so it needs the past tense.

questions.q: Passage 14 — We had booked a small hotel near the town centre, which was own by a retired teacher.
questions.tip: The error was “own”. After 'was' the passive needs the past participle 'owned'.

questions.q: Passage 14 — On the first evening we walk along the river and watched the boats go past.
questions.tip: The error was “walk”. It must match the past tense of 'watched' in the same sentence.

questions.q: Passage 14 — My sister said that the food there was gooder than anything at home.
questions.tip: The error was “gooder”. The comparative of 'good' is 'better'.

questions.q: Passage 14 — Between the two of us, I was the most adventurous eater.
questions.tip: The error was “most”. With only two people, use the comparative 'more'.

questions.q: Passage 14 — All the stalls had they own speciality.
questions.tip: The error was “they”. A possessive is needed before 'own'.

questions.q: Passage 14 — We looked forward to bring the pineapple tarts home to our grandparents.
questions.tip: The error was “bring”. After 'look forward to' the verb takes the -ing form.

questions.q: Passage 14 — The hotel owner showed us a museum that we would never had found alone.
questions.tip: The error was “had”. After 'would' the verb is 'have'.

questions.q: Passage 14 — By the time we left, all of us was sunburnt and happy.
questions.tip: The error was “was”. 'All of us' is plural.

questions.q: Passage 15 — Our school held it's annual cross-country race last Friday.
questions.tip: The error was “it's”. 'It's' means 'it is'; the possessive has no apostrophe.

questions.q: Passage 15 — Neither the Primary 5 nor the Primary 6 pupils was allowed to skip it.
questions.tip: The error was “was”. With 'neither … nor' the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'pupils'.

questions.q: Passage 15 — I had been training for weeks, so I feel confident at the starting line.
questions.tip: The error was “feel”. The sentence is in the past tense.

questions.q: Passage 15 — The route was longer as I had expected.
questions.tip: The error was “as”. A comparative such as 'longer' is followed by 'than'.

questions.q: Passage 15 — By the second kilometre my legs was aching badly.
questions.tip: The error was “was”. 'Legs' is plural.

questions.q: Passage 15 — A boy in front of me trip over a tree root and fell heavily.
questions.tip: The error was “trip”. The past tense is needed to match 'fell'.

questions.q: Passage 15 — I stopped to help him, although the other runners were overtake us.
questions.tip: The error was “overtake”. After 'were' the verb takes the -ing form.

questions.q: Passage 15 — We finished last, but our form teacher said she were proud of us.
questions.tip: The error was “were”. 'She' takes 'was'.

questions.q: Passage 15 — Since that day, the boy and me have trained together every Tuesday.
questions.tip: The error was “me”. It is part of the subject of the sentence.

questions.q: Passage 16 — The public library near my flat have four floors.
questions.tip: The error was “have”. 'The library' is singular.

questions.q: Passage 16 — On the top floor there is a quiet room where nobody are allowed to speak.
questions.tip: The error was “are”. 'Nobody' is singular.

questions.q: Passage 16 — I have went there every Saturday since January.
questions.tip: The error was “went”. After 'have' the past participle is 'gone'.

questions.q: Passage 16 — Last week I borrowed three book about volcanoes.
questions.tip: The error was “book”. 'Three' requires the plural.

questions.q: Passage 16 — The librarian, Mr Suresh, recommend a fourth one to me.
questions.tip: The error was “recommend”. The sentence is in the past tense.

questions.q: Passage 16 — He said that it were the best book on the subject in the whole collection.
questions.tip: The error was “were”. 'It' takes 'was'.

questions.q: Passage 16 — I finished reading it in two days, which is quicker then I usually manage.
questions.tip: The error was “then”. After a comparative use 'than'.

questions.q: Passage 16 — My younger brother, who dislike reading, asked to borrow it next.
questions.tip: The error was “dislike”. 'Who' refers to 'brother', which is singular.

questions.q: Passage 16 — Now the two of us goes to the library together.
questions.tip: The error was “goes”. 'The two of us' is plural.

questions.q: Passage 17 — Every morning the cleaners at our school starts work at half past five.
questions.tip: The error was “starts”. 'The cleaners' is plural.

questions.q: Passage 17 — By the time we arrive, the corridors has already been mopped.
questions.tip: The error was “has”. 'Corridors' is plural.

questions.q: Passage 17 — Last term our class decide to write them a thank-you card.
questions.tip: The error was “decide”. 'Last term' requires the past tense.

questions.q: Passage 17 — We were surprised how little we knowed about them.
questions.tip: The error was “knowed”. The past tense of 'know' is 'knew'.

questions.q: Passage 17 — Mdm Siti, the cleaner on our floor, have three grandchildren.
questions.tip: The error was “have”. 'Mdm Siti' is singular.

questions.q: Passage 17 — Every day she wake up at four o'clock to catch the first bus.
questions.tip: The error was “wake”. 'She' takes the -s form for a habit.

questions.q: Passage 17 — None of us had ever thought to ask her nothing about her life.
questions.tip: The error was “nothing”. Two negatives in one clause cancel each other out.

questions.q: Passage 17 — Since then, our class have kept its own floor tidy.
questions.tip: The error was “have”. 'Its' shows the class is being treated as one body, so the verb is 'has'.

questions.q: Passage 17 — It is the least we could of done.
questions.tip: The error was “of”. The phrase is 'could have done'.

sets.title: Grammar cloze · two more passages
sets.instruction: One word only for each blank. Read the whole passage first.

passages.text:
Passage A — The Sports Day That Nearly Was

Sports Day (1)______ supposed to begin at eight.

By seven, most (2)______ the classes had already gathered on the field.

The tents were up (3)______ the loudspeakers had been tested.

(4)______ the sky turned the colour of wet cement.

(5)______ ten minutes the first drops had fallen.

Eight hundred pupils (6)______ hurried back into the hall.

We sat there (7)______ almost an hour, listening to the rain on the roof.

(8)______ said very much.

Some of us had (9)______ training since March.

(10)______ twenty past nine, Mr Raj came to the microphone.

He announced (11)______ the races would be held indoors instead.

The relay (12)______ not be run, but everything else went ahead.

The hall was noisier (13)______ the field would ever have been.

We finished at noon, (14)______ was earlier than planned.

Nobody complained, and neither (15)______ the teachers.

Passage B — The Kitchen Rule

My grandmother (16)______ cooked in the same kitchen for forty years.

There is just (17)______ rule in it, and only one.

Anybody (18)______ eats must also wash something.

It (19)______ not matter what you wash.

A single spoon counts (20)______ much as a wok.

(21)______ I was six, I thought the rule was unfair.

I complained (22)______ my cousins always chose the spoons.

My grandmother (23)______ me that I was free to choose a spoon too.

I did, and (24)______ took me several years to notice what she had done.

(25)______ in that kitchen works, so nobody is a guest.

I have (26)______ washing up in there since before I could reach the tap.

(27)______ my youngest cousin stands on the same wooden stool.

He does not know that the rule is (28)______ way of keeping us all in the room.

The kitchen is the only place (29)______ our whole family talks.

I think she (30)______ say that is the point.

answers.tip: 'Sports Day was supposed to begin' — a singular subject in the past takes 'was'.
'Most of the classes' needs 'of' to link the amount to the group.
Two completed preparations are joined, so a simple addition word is needed.
A sentence-opening time word is needed to move the story on to what happened next.
'Within ten minutes' gives the period inside which the rain started.
'Eight hundred pupils' is plural, so the past tense takes 'were'.
A length of time after 'sat there' takes 'for'.
A negative subject is needed: nobody said much, because everyone was disappointed.
'Had been training since March' — a period running up to that day takes the past perfect continuous.
A clock time takes 'at': at twenty past nine.
'He announced that…' introduces reported speech.
'Could not be run' — the passive after a modal.
'Noisier' is a comparative, so it takes 'than'.
'Which' refers back to the whole idea of finishing at noon.
'Neither did the teachers' — the negative agreement pattern inverts with 'did'.
The present perfect is needed for cooking that began forty years ago and still goes on.
'Just one rule' — the number is what 'and only one' repeats.
'Anybody who eats' — 'who' introduces the relative clause about a person.
'It does not matter' — the negative of 'matter' in the present tense.
'Counts as much as' is the set comparison phrase.
A time clause about the past is needed: when the narrator was six.
A reason is being given for the complaint, so a causal connector fits.
'Told me that' — 'tell' takes a person as its object.
'It took me several years' — the impersonal 'it' begins the clause.
A subject meaning every person in the kitchen is needed to match 'so nobody is a guest'.
'Have been washing up since…' — an action continuing from the past until now.
A present-time word contrasts the cousin now with the narrator at six.
A possessive is needed before 'way of keeping us all in the room'.
'The only place where' — 'where' introduces a clause about a place.
'I think she would say' — a reported opinion about what she might say.
